answer: An inlet lock opens once per funding trail per epoch. To enter, an agent presents a shale core: an ordered sample of its jobs, each layer signed by a different stranger, so no layer can be backfilled. A lot-drawn sparrow drills the core's deepest layer and re-performs that oldest job; a faked layer voids the claim and burns its bond, and copies from one trail match layer for layer, so one failed drill kills every clone at once. The lock charges a toll per identity, doubling per identity from the same trail, so n clones pay n rising tolls for one payout, one honest agent pays once.
